meta.note: Month-by-month jobs tailored to Alex's actual plant list. UK / Scotland-ish timing — shift a week or two later for a cold spring. Always confirm clematis pruning group before cutting.

jobs: Prune roses on a mild day
Cut back pampas grass (gloves!) before new growth
Mulch beds while soil is bare
Top-dress + feed roses, fruit trees, wisteria
Watch lily beetle (red) on emerging lilies
Plant out tender herbs once frost risk passes
Tie in clematis + climbing rose laterals horizontally
Move/protect lemon verbena + olives if late frost
Trim lavender lightly as first flush fades
Keep new plantings watered — sun-trap dries fast
First wisteria summer prune — whippy growth to ~5 buds
Prune fig (after fruiting); protect next year's embryo figs later
Plant spring bulbs: crocus, daffs, alliums
Cut back faded perennials (leave echinacea seedheads for goldfinches)
Lift gladioli corms after first frost in a cold year
Clear fallen fruit (apple/pear) to reduce disease
Wrap/move olives + fig if hard frost forecast
Leave alliums + grasses standing for winter structure
Tidy, but leave seedheads for birds
Winter-prune apple/pear on a dry day

rules_of_thumb: Lavender, broom, curry plant: never cut into old bare wood — they don't reshoot.
Wisteria: two prunes a year (Jul/Aug to ~5 buds, Jan/Feb to ~2 buds) = best flowering.
Clematis: confirm pruning group (1/2/3) before cutting — getting it wrong loses a year of flower.
Cherry + plum-family: prune in summer, not winter, to dodge silver leaf.
Leave echinacea + allium seedheads standing — food + structure.
Sun-trap = fast drying. The Gardena Back Garden probe hit 10% — prioritise water there in heat.
